title: Keyturn Roadside Assistance: Suspension, Lapse and Reinstatement of Cover
content:
## Standing of a subscription

Cover is suspended where the fee goes unpaid or where the pattern of callouts puts the subscription in
front of a reviewer, and the member is told which of the two it is.

Cover falls away where the fee stays unpaid past the plan's lapse period, counted in whole calendar
days from the day it fell due, and a lapse may be put right inside the plan's reinstatement window on
payment of the plan's reinstatement fee.

A reinstated subscription runs to the renewal date it already had rather than starting a fresh term, so
reinstatement restores cover without buying more of it.

### The two grounds of suspension

| Ground | What the member is told |
| --- | --- |
| The subscription fee has gone unpaid | That the suspension is for the unpaid fee |
| The pattern of callouts puts the subscription in front of a reviewer | That the suspension is for the review |

The clause requires the member to be told which of the two grounds applies, so the two are never left
undistinguished. A suspension is recorded against a Keyturn Roadside Assistance subscription whose own
record stands in the active state or in the suspended state, that record carrying the authority and the
subscription's reference number tying it to the suspension; the point is settled before the suspension
is made.

### The lapse clock and the reinstatement window

The lapse period is counted in whole calendar days from the day the fee fell due, and cover falls away
where the fee is still unpaid past that period. A lapse may then be put right inside the plan's
reinstatement window, on payment of the plan's reinstatement fee. What reinstatement restores is the
term that was already running: the subscription runs to the renewal date it already had, and no
further term is bought by reinstating.
